# Provider Operating System architecture

Baseline: cb83c0316f7fb709d026c52c727db2ba209fe817 (actual fetched main, merged PR #37). Branch: codex/provider-operating-system. Existing clean focused worktree reused; no second worktree created. Root/recovery trees are preserved.

The canonical AI registry still owns adapter definitions, discovery, health and models. Router V2 still owns selection and fallback. Provider OS adds scoped profile configuration and safe server projections inside `src/lib/ai/provider-os`; it does not add a provider registry or generation runtime. Coding-agent detection stays behind the existing authenticated local bridge. Detection never authorizes agent execution.

Profile identity is a UUID, scoped by authenticated owner and owned workspace. Personal workspace identity is derived from the authenticated user; request bodies cannot choose the owner. Server-only service-role writes prevent direct browser policy escalation. Safe metadata SELECT uses ownership RLS. Credentials, including ciphertext, have no browser-role grants.

AES-256-GCM envelopes bind owner/workspace/credential identity as authenticated additional data. The 32-byte master key is server-only, separate from the database. No auto-generated or public key is persisted. Missing secure-store configuration blocks credential writes. Existing environment operators remain supported without schema-dependent startup. Environment references are limited to the provider's declared variable names and authorized operators. Profile credentials override only that provider's declared auth source, never global process.env.

Atomic service-role transactions implement profile activation, optimistic-version updates, credential replacement/rotation/revocation, invalidation of dependent runtime evidence, dependency-aware credential deletion and safe audit IDs/events. Profile deletion retains credentials. Database foreign keys bind shared references to the same provider/owner/workspace. No audit field can contain request payloads or plaintext values.

Public Next.js code does not execute CLI commands or enumerate arbitrary host environment. The existing trusted bridge supplies bounded binary/version and installed MCP/plugin/skill metadata. Capability support, profile permission policy and current executor availability remain independent. No connection is fabricated from a configured name.

The browser renders a bounded full intelligence catalog; Build eligibility is a derived filter, not a destructive catalog mutation. OpenRouter is a gateway. FREE requires both measured input/output prices equal zero. Unknown usage, quota and cost stay UNKNOWN, and provider-reported account data remains distinct from KNOuX-measured request data.

Additive migration is generated by Supabase CLI. It is validated against local PostgreSQL-compatible PGlite before delivery; hosted installation and key provisioning are reported separately. Rollback: disable the Provider OS route/profile selection and keep the legacy canonical environment runtime; preserve encrypted credential/profile/audit tables for recovery. Never drop or cascade credential data as a rollback. Before retiring a master key, rotate/re-encrypt every reference and keep previous key IDs server-side until verified.

Documentation consulted: Supabase RLS and API grants, September 2026 PostgreSQL minor-release notes (no legacy PGP encryption used), OpenRouter model metadata API, and the installed Next.js 16.3.8 route-handler/server-client/CSS guides.

## Installation and operating boundaries

Apply the additive `20261008234936_provider_operating_system.sql` migration through the authorized Supabase migration process. Configure `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` and the server-only `KNOUX_PROVIDER_VAULT_KEY` (canonical base64 encoding of a securely generated 32-byte key), with an optional `KNOUX_PROVIDER_VAULT_KEY_ID`. Do not use a public environment variable, repository file or browser storage for either key. Provisioning those credentials and applying the hosted migration are deployment operations, not automatic application startup steps. Existing environment-only operators can continue to use the canonical adapters when persistence is unavailable.

The authenticated `/api/build/provider-os` endpoint returns owned metadata only. Its bounded POST command API supports workspace creation/selection, profile creation/update/activation/deletion, credential creation/replacement/rotation/revocation/dependency-aware deletion, nonbillable connection testing and explicitly acknowledged live testing. Header workspace selection is validated server-side; successful selection sets an HttpOnly cookie scoped to `/api/build`. The same scope feeds canonical generation, streaming, arena, routing, preparation, provider, discovery and usage routes. Failed/stale mutations are not retried automatically. Missing configuration still exposes canonical provider definitions with an explicit blocker and empty private records.

Default TEST CONNECTION calls authentication and model discovery; it never calls generation. RUN LIVE GENERATION TEST requires an explicit `billingAcknowledged: true`; the additional streaming test requires a separate `streamingAcknowledged: true`. These use fixed tiny prompts and discard generated content. Requested provider/model, actual model, token counts, latency, streaming completion and cost basis remain separate. A successful metadata call cannot promote runtime capability to VERIFIED. Regular canonical runtime results also persist measured connection facts with profile-version checks; key replacement cannot be overwritten by a stale in-flight result.

Custom remote endpoints require HTTPS, an exact server `KNOUX_PROVIDER_ALLOWED_HOSTS` allowlist, public DNS results and pinned connections without redirects. Local loopback endpoints are refused on hosted deployments and restricted to server `KNOUX_PROVIDER_LOCAL_PORTS` (defaults 11434, 1234, 8080). Native binaries are inspected only by the trusted, owner-paired bridge. Operator-side `KNOUX_PROVIDER_AGENT_BINARIES` can declare approved absolute BUNDLED/CUSTOM binary references; BUNDLED references must stay inside the bridge project root. Inspection executes fixed version arguments, never submitted shell text. Installed project MCP/skills/plugins are measured from bounded local metadata, with environment variable names only.

Agent permission policy defaults to DENY. Non-DENY updates require an authorized operator and the exact ceiling in server `KNOUX_AGENT_PERMISSION_CEILING`. A stored ASK/ALLOW policy does not install an executor or prove capability support. Bindings require observed inventory identities; working-directory references must be the owned workspace UUID. Agent execution, subagents, worktrees, terminal, commit and push remain unavailable until a real agent executor is implemented and paired. Global user plugin caches are not claimed as project installations.

KNOuX usage is measured in an isolated owner/workspace ledger retained within the running server instance (bounded instances and 10,000 retained operations). It is not durable billing enforcement or the provider's bill. Setting a monthly spending ceiling blocks automatic/manual profile routing while durable enforcement is unavailable. OpenRouter account usage is projected only from numeric fields returned by its authenticated `/key` API. Balances, reset times and unsupported provider metrics remain UNKNOWN; deprecated gateway rate-limit fields are not treated as quota.

## Evidence and deployment blockers

The unchanged merged baseline passed 747 local tests and the full production-browser suite (529 passed, 32 conditional skips). Its development/tooling audit already reports six high advisories; production dependency audit passes. No gate was weakened to mask these findings.

The implementation is covered by actual local SQL/RLS/atomicity tests, scoped canonical runtime and transport tests, real bridge HTTP ticket/inventory tests, and explicitly labelled browser contract fixtures. Browser contract fixtures prove interaction/layout only; they do not prove hosted persistence, provider authentication or agent execution. Twelve exact viewport captures include provider center, profiles, credentials, catalog, usage, diagnostics, permissions, installed bindings and mobile provider disclosure. Additional captures distinguish real anonymous AUTH_REQUIRED from labelled fixture refusal states.

Nonbillable canonical auth/discovery measured on 2026-10-09 succeeded for OpenAI (127 catalog / 76 Build candidates), Gemini (62 / 45), Groq (11 / 7), Mistral (46 / 27), DeepSeek direct (2 / 2), and Grok via OpenRouter (8 / 8). Anthropic returned INVALID_REQUEST. OpenRouter, Qwen, OpenCode Go, Ollama and LM Studio were blocked by measured network failures. Custom OpenAI was unconfigured. No provider account, billing plan or subscription was changed. Generation and streaming were not executed without the mission's required separate cost acknowledgement.

Read-only deployment preflight found no service-role credential and no vault master key in the legitimate local configuration. Therefore hosted schema availability and real hosted profile/credential writes are UNTESTED/BLOCKED, not operationally verified. No hosted migration or resource creation was performed. Secret-value scanning uses authorized values in memory, prints no values, and compares candidate sources, browser bundles and QA logs. Final exact-head local/GitHub status, artifacts and remaining blockers are reported on the single delivery PR; this branch must not be auto-merged.
